stem:
Gopal studies a regular hexagon with centre $O$ marked at the meeting point of lines joining opposite vertices.

Does the hexagon have rotational symmetry?

options.text: Yes, because a turn of $60^{\circ}$ about $O$ makes the hexagon coincide with itself, and $60^{\circ}$ is less than a full turn.
Say the centre $O$ is what the matching turn creates.
Yes, because counting the six vertices of the hexagon decides that it has rotational symmetry.

teacher.key_rationale: A 60° turn about O maps the regular hexagon onto itself and is less than 360°, so it has rotational symmetry. Calling O the name rotational symmetry swaps terms. Saying the turn creates the centre reverses the relation. Settling the question by counting vertices alone conflates another mechanism.
